rationale: Restored execution citations that the current accounts rely on but whose newest revisions had dropped: the repair-path interpretation's text uses the healed-divergence receipt and the child account's text uses the split, healing, applied-state, control, per-node-repair and long-run/configuration-change receipts, while their latest execution maps cited only the newest few. This is a citation-coherence repair; conclusions, defect judgments and limits are unchanged, and the earlier revisions still hold their own citations.

interpretations.joint_history: Five receipts of five fixed experiments over the same divergent state: fa1f90c2eefd45e6af45d7593ac53205 records the healed divergence in which the entry and applied state differ across nodes; 112186e8b9544b51b4f7818a04c78a84 adds the per-node repair phase in which a lagging restarted node installs a snapshot; 6ff0ef691a0141449142bfa06719bb47 further revises that harness so the leader consumes a snapshot through the Restore contract; 861a2b3c62bb44d7aed2eee9b95aa15f shows the divergence surviving a long run and 182740a6d29f4af9a99cf83c49f2e857 shows it surviving a configuration change. All five observe the same cluster identity, conflict index and payloads (minority-write against majority-write at index 11, term 3), and each comparison outcome is read from its own receipt.
interpretations.rationale: Answer: the divergence left by this defect is reconciled by replacing the node's state, not by ordinary log comparison, and only two of the three candidate mechanisms actually apply. The healed divergence itself is recorded in receipt fa1f90c2eefd45e6af45d7593ac53205 (index 3: different payloads at the conflict index and different applied writes across nodes). A node that falls behind a compacted leader is sent a snapshot and ends up with the leader's FSM state, entry suffix and configuration (receipt 112186e8b9544b51b4f7818a04c78a84, index 4), repairing that node only. A leader-side restore converges the cluster (receipt 6ff0ef691a0141449142bfa06719bb47, index 5, where all five applied write lists agree and the minority write is gone). The long-run and configuration-change receipts (861a2b3c62bb44d7aed2eee9b95aa15f index 3, 182740a6d29f4af9a99cf83c49f2e857 index 4) show that neither the entry nor the applied state is reconciled while the node keeps up. Truncation by a different term does not arise: the conflicting entries are at the highest index of every log at the same term and vote admission requires a candidate's log to be at least as up to date as the voter's (raft.go 1725-1750), so a later leader can only append beyond that index where same-term duplicates are skipped (raft.go 1526-1553). Remaining limits: the per-node repair needed harness-arranged lag and the restore used a snapshot the leader produced itself; samples are single per mode with in-memory stores and scaled timeouts; the term-truncation route is argued unavailable rather than tested.
limitations: The per-node repair needed harness-arranged lag and the cluster-wide repair used a snapshot the leader produced itself.
Single samples per mode with in-memory stores and scaled timeouts.
The term-truncation route is argued unavailable from the vote rule rather than tested; a variant of the defect that left a shorter log on a node able to win votes could change that.
counterevidence: Without either replacement mechanism the long-run and configuration-change receipts show the divergence persisting, so neither path is engaged by ordinary operation while the node keeps up.
The per-node repair leaves an up-to-date divergent node untouched, whereas the restore converges the cluster, so the two mechanisms are not interchangeable.

interpretations.joint_history: Eight receipts of seven fixed experiments over one defect chain, sharing the structural fixture (snapshot configuration {A,B,C}, a committed configuration entry with {A,B,C,D,E} above it, a persisted commit index covering it) and the feature-on restart reporting {A,B,C} against the control reporting {A,B,C,D,E}. They successively construct the restart state, observe the split (b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e), add the healing phase (455e647ad0794a16903414b5a8846276), add applied-state sampling (fa1f90c2eefd45e6af45d7593ac53205), add the per-node repair phase (112186e8b9544b51b4f7818a04c78a84), run both restart modes (531b0a48500843228e26623ce7333943), extend to a long run (861a2b3c62bb44d7aed2eee9b95aa15f), add a configuration change (182740a6d29f4af9a99cf83c49f2e857) and exercise the leader-side restore (6ff0ef691a0141449142bfa06719bb47). Each comparison outcome is read from its own receipt, and each revision restricted its comparison set to new predicates.
interpretations.rationale: Answer: yes, with both consequences bounded and the repair options identified. Receipt b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e records the split: the restarted node reports {A,B,C} (index 1), leads the two-voter partition while the other three voters elect their own leader (index 2, leader_count 2) and both sides commit at the same index and term. Receipt 455e647ad0794a16903414b5a8846276 shows the divergent entries surviving healing, fa1f90c2eefd45e6af45d7593ac53205 shows the applied state differing afterwards, and the control receipt 531b0a48500843228e26623ce7333943 shows that with the feature off the same restart reports {A,B,C,D,E}, elects no minority leader and applies nothing of its own. The long-run and configuration-change receipts (861a2b3c62bb44d7aed2eee9b95aa15f index 3, 182740a6d29f4af9a99cf83c49f2e857 index 4) show the entry and applied divergence surviving a long run and a membership change, while the stale membership itself ends at that configuration change. The divergence is removed only by replacement: per node by a snapshot install (receipt 112186e8b9544b51b4f7818a04c78a84 index 4) or cluster-wide by a leader-side restore (receipt 6ff0ef691a0141449142bfa06719bb47 index 5). Remaining limits: the configuration change was a single harness-issued AddVoter; the long run is entry-count based; the per-node repair needed harness-arranged lag and the restore used a self-produced snapshot; ordinary log comparison is argued unable to reconcile the divergence from the vote rule rather than tested; and in-memory stores with scaled timeouts were used.
limitations: The configuration change is a single harness-issued AddVoter and the long run is ~200 entries without a snapshot install.
The per-node repair needed harness-arranged lag and the cluster-wide repair used a snapshot the leader produced itself.
Ordinary log comparison is argued unable to reconcile the divergence from the vote rule rather than tested.
In-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown rather than a crash.
counterevidence: The feature-off control run over the identical scenario, long run, configuration change and restore shows no stale membership, no minority leader and no self-applied write.
A later configuration entry ends the stale membership, and both replacement paths remove the divergent entry and applied state.
Without a replacement the earlier receipts show the divergence persisting while the node keeps up, so the consequences are bounded by repair timing rather than by ordinary operation.
